optionalSupplies: A toy or a pea-sized piece of their usual food
substitutes: No towel? An old T-shirt works for paws.
title: First Snow, First Footprints
clue: The first marks on a blank morning are your dog's, and your job is to read them.
reveal: On the first snow day, or any morning where pawprints show (soft frost, mud, damp sand), your dog goes first across untouched ground. Then you walk the trail beside their prints and read it like a detective: the sniff stop, the little loop, the trot.
objective: Let your dog make the first tracks on a quiet patch of untouched ground, then walk back beside the trail and read what they did.
instructions: Choose your day: first real snow, or any morning where prints show (a light frost, soft mud after rain, damp earth, a dusting). Check conditions and your dog's comfort before you go; ice, cold or heat means a shorter version or skipping it.
Find the nearest untouched patch: your yard, a quiet corner of a green, a field edge, away from roads and ice, with a clear way home.

Stop at the edge. In a fenced yard let your dog roam; in public, keep them on a leash and walk beside rather than behind. Let them go first and choose where to trot, sniff or stand. Stay off their trail so you do not trample it.
Give them a few minutes, then step off to the side so the trail stays clean.

Read the trail: walk back along its edge from start to finish like a detective: 'here, the big sniff; here, the loop; here, the sudden trot; here, the sit'. Say each one aloud and give each bend a name.
The surprise (optional): at the end, pile a little snow or leaf litter over a favorite toy or a pea-sized crumb of their usual food, and let them dig it up if they like.
Look back from the start at the whole trail, name the bends and take one photo. Then towel off, wipe paws and let your dog warm up and rest.
twist: You follow, not leash: the map is made entirely by your dog, and you read it afterwards like a detective story about a morning you thought you knew.
variations: No snow: use soft frost, mud, damp earth or a dusting of fine soil in a yard bed; the reading is the same.
Window version: watch from a window as your dog makes first tracks in the yard, then step out together to read them for a minute.
Senior, small or thin-coated: a few minutes on a patch beside the door, with a coat if they already wear one.
Bigger version: a quiet park or field after a snowfall that you can walk to, on a leash and clear of roads and sledders.
completion: Counts when your dog has made tracks (or simply stood on the fresh ground) and you have looked back along them and named at least one bend.
photoIdea: The whole trail seen from its start, taken low, with your dog at the end or beside it.
memoryPrompt: What was the first thing your dog did on untouched ground, and which bend did you name?
dietNotes: Optional only: a pea-sized piece of the food your dog already eats, from the day's ration. Ask your vet about diet limits. A toy makes it no-food.
safety: Skip icy or hard-frozen paths and head home on shivering, a tucked tail or lifted paws.
Wipe paws after salt or de-icer, keep clear of frozen water, and only use food your dog already eats.
Puppies: stay with the home or yard version until your vet says public places are fine.
